h1: Break of Structure (BOS): Rules and Limits
quickAnswer: A break of structure (BOS) is a qualifying break of a selected swing in the direction of an established swing sequence. A bullish BOS clears a prior high in an upward sequence; a bearish BOS clears a prior low in a downward sequence. This lesson requires a completed close strictly beyond the level. That is a stated convention, not a universal rule or a promise that the trend will continue.
takeaways: Name the trend, the swing and the confirmation rule before naming a BOS.
A wick, a close beyond the level and a later successful continuation are three different observations.
A confirmed BOS can fail later. Keep the original event in the journal instead of moving the reference to rescue the idea.
Displacement, an FVG and a retest are extra conditions only when your written model requires them.

sections.title: 1. What is a break of structure in trading?

blocks.text: Imagine price has made highs of 110.00 and 120.00, with lows of 100.00 and 108.00. The highs and lows have both moved upward. If the selected next candle closes at 122.00 above the fixed high of 120.00, the upward sequence has extended under our close-based rule. This is the event we call a bullish BOS. It describes what just happened; it does not reveal what must happen next.

The useful question is not whether a candle looks powerful. It is: which previously identified reference did it break, on which chart, using which test? A large green candle inside a range may break nothing relevant. A modest candle can close beyond a well-defined swing. Context and measurement come before the label.

blocks.text: Start with Swing Highs and Lows and Internal vs External Market Structure. A pivot is a local turning point; its role in the larger sequence is a separate choice. For these examples, a strict three-bar high is higher than the highs immediately before and after it. It becomes known only when the third bar closes. Equal highs do not pass that strict test. Other pivot rules are valid study choices if declared and used consistently.

With highs of 118.00, 120.00 and 117.00, the middle high qualifies after bar 3 closes. Draw the reference forward from that recognition time. Do not let an indicator place an arrow on bar 2 and then assume you could act on it while bar 2 was forming. TradingView’s Williams fractal uses a different, normally five-bar construction; its confirmation delay illustrates why settings matter.

sections.title: 4. How to identify a BOS, step by step

items: Set the map: record the illustrative upward sequence 100.00 → 110.00 → 108.00 → 120.00. Do not infer a trend from one candle.
Freeze the reference: mark the confirmed 120.00 high and the 108.00 structural low. The smaller 116.00 pullback is an internal reference, not an automatic replacement for 108.00.
Declare the rule: require a completed five-minute close strictly above 120.00. A high of 123.00 with a close of 119.00 does not qualify; a close of exactly 120.00 is only a touch.
Record the event: the bar opening at 10:10 closes at 10:15 America/New_York. Its 122.00 close is 2.00 points beyond the reference. Before 10:15, a close-based decision is unfinished.
Separate follow-through: later prices may hold above 120.00, reclaim below it or never retest it. Journal those outcomes separately from the original BOS.

sections.title: 5. Does a BOS require a wick or a candle close?

blocks.text: There is no universal naming standard across educators and indicators. Our default test is close > reference for a bullish break and close < reference for a bearish break. A close outside does not mean the entire candle body must be outside. A candle opening at 119.00 and closing at 122.00 passes the bullish test at 120.00 even though part of its body remains below the line.

ICT’s selected Episode 3 example allows trading above the referenced high before a close, then examines the completed FVG separately. Episode 6 gives more weight to an energetic move and a preferred close in its bearish-shift discussion. These are source-specific teaching contexts. Neither passage justifies saying every BOS everywhere must use one identical confirmation rule.

sections.title: 6. Worked example: a break followed by a hold

blocks.text: All prices below are invented for an illustrative index. Timeframe: five minutes. Time zone: America/New_York. No historical trading date is implied. The pre-existing upward map is 100.00 → 110.00 → 108.00 → 120.00. The table begins after the selected 120.00 swing has already been confirmed; it is not a complete reconstruction of that earlier leg.

At 10:10 the first bar’s high of 121.00 has crossed 120.00, but its 119.00 close has not. At 10:15 the next bar closes at 122.00, so the close-based BOS qualifies. At 10:20, a low of 120.50 and close of 123.00 show a pullback that stayed above the reference. The final close of 125.00 is follow-through in this authored case, not a success rate.

sections.title: 7. Contrasting example: a confirmed break that fails

blocks.text: Keep the first two bars unchanged, including the qualifying 122.00 close. Replace the later path with the failure bars below. The 10:15 bar closes at 118.00 at 10:20, back beneath 120.00. The next close reaches 115.00. The event at 10:15 was still a BOS under the written rule; the expectation that price would remain above 120.00 failed afterward.

Do not redraw the reference at 118.00 and describe the earlier break as flawless. A descriptive label can be valid while a trade loses. Also distinguish reclaiming the broken high from breaking the larger structural low of 108.00: the former weakens this local continuation idea; it does not by itself complete a bearish external reversal.

sections.title: 8. Internal BOS, external BOS and timeframe conflict

blocks.text: A five-minute bullish BOS above 120.00 can sit inside an hourly downward leg bounded by 140.00 and 100.00. The small upward sequence extended; the hourly 140.00 reference remains intact. Write both statements. Do not promote a small break into a higher-timeframe reversal because the smaller drawing looks cleaner.

A range needs different language. Repeated crossings between 118.00 and 122.00 may be range-edge breaks rather than continuation of an established trend. Select the range first; record failed attempts and costs. More labels do not create more evidence.

Neither an indicator’s label nor an acronym establishes who traded. Avoid a universal ladder in which CHoCH always becomes MSS and MSS always becomes a profitable reversal.

sections.title: 10. Does BOS need displacement, an FVG or a retest?

blocks.text: Separate three checklists. Geometry asks whether the selected level broke. A setup filter may ask for displacement or a fair value gap. An execution rule may require a return to that gap at a planned price. Passing the first checklist does not pass the other two. A large body does not prove an FVG; its three-candle outer ranges must satisfy the gap definition.

For a hypothetical limit-entry study, entry 120.50, stop 117.50 and target 126.50 imply 3.00 points of price risk and 6.00 points of reward, or 2R before costs. If price never returns to 120.50, the result is unfilled, not a captured 2R. If one OHLC bar touches both stop and target, the sequence is unknown without finer data. The numbers are invented arithmetic, not an entry recommendation.

A premium/discount filter is another optional model choice. For an invented selected leg from 108.00 to 126.00, equilibrium is (108.00 + 126.00) / 2 = 117.00. Prices below 117.00 are the lower half of that leg; they are not objectively cheap or automatically safe. An order block is a separately selected candle reference. Neither a discount label nor an order-block label rescues a missing break, an unfilled entry or a failed risk rule.

sections.title: 11. How to mark BOS on a chart without hindsight

items: Choose the instrument, feed, timeframe and time zone; use ordinary OHLC candles rather than treating synthetic candle types as traded prices.
Use a horizontal ray at the confirmed swing price, write the recognition time in its label, and keep the reference fixed during replay.
Reveal one completed bar at a time. Log high/low, close, event time and any separate setup filters before revealing the outcome.
Use Chart Lab for evidence marking and Backtest Lab for a written rule record. Do not treat the authored exercises as a representative market sample.

sections.title: 16. The useful limit of a BOS label

blocks.text: A BOS is most useful when it makes your observation reproducible: the same map, the same line, the same time and the same test. It becomes less useful when it is asked to predict a destination or explain invisible motives. Carry the fixed map into the next chapter, Change of Character, and ask what changes when the first break points the other way.

faqs.question: What is a break of structure (BOS) in trading?
faqs.answer: It is a qualifying break of a selected swing with the established sequence. Under this lesson’s convention, the candle must close strictly beyond the reference. It records a structural event, not a guaranteed future continuation.

faqs.question: How do you use break of structure in trading?
faqs.answer: Use it to organise a map, then apply separately written setup, entry, invalidation and risk rules. A BOS alone does not select an entry or a position size. In practice exercises, record skipped and unfilled cases as well as qualifying breaks.

faqs.question: Does a BOS need a candle close?
faqs.answer: This lesson requires one, but naming conventions differ. An intrabar-high crossing and a completed close are different tests. State which one you use before reviewing the outcome; do not switch between them after a loss.

faqs.question: What is the difference between BOS and CHoCH?
faqs.answer: Here, BOS extends the selected existing sequence; CHoCH is the first qualifying break of its selected opposing swing. Both depend on scale and reference choice. Neither label alone proves a lasting new trend.

faqs.question: Does price always retest a BOS?
faqs.answer: No. A retest is a possible later path, not part of this basic break definition. A plan that requires a return can remain unfilled. Do not retrospectively replace the missed limit entry with a chase.

faqs.question: Which timeframe is best for BOS?
faqs.answer: No universal best timeframe is established here. Smaller bars reveal more local events and can be more sensitive to feed differences and costs. Choose a timeframe for a defined study and keep its rules fixed when comparing cases.

terms.definition: A qualifying break with the selected existing swing sequence.
A previously identified swing whose price is tested by the break rule.
Trading beyond a level without necessarily closing beyond it.
Price returning across a previously broken reference.
A planned entry price was not reached under the execution rule.
